info.title: Edgematrix EdgeAI box API device manager ⚙️
info.description:
## Overview
This microservice provides APIs to check and change
the configuration of the edge AI device itself and
to reboot the device itself.

## Actions
Using these APIs, users can perform the following operations:

- **Reboot the device**.
- **Change the clock time**.
- **Change the time zone**.
- **Enable or disable NTP**.
- **Setup IP settings**.
- **Manage user accounts and M2M tokens for the Web UI**.

Only users who belong to the admin group can
perform this operation.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the GPG key file is not found, a 500 error

get.description:
Reads all user account information registered in this device.

No parameters are required for this request.

Users belonging to the admin group or M2M authentication can
view information for all user accounts, while users belonging
to the operator and guest groups can view only their own
user accounts.
If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this API, a 403
error will be returned.

Reads all currently registered user information from a file
and returns it in dictionary format. The keys of the
dictionary are user names and the values are user information.
User information includes the following:
- accounttype: Indicates whether the account is user or token
information. Since this API handles only user information,
user is always returned.
- creation: The date and time the user was created.
- expire: Accounts that expire after this time are
automatically deactivated. Accounts with no expiration date will
be displayed as `perpetual`.
- disabled: True if the account is disabled, false if the
account is enabled.
- expired: True if the account is expired, false otherwise.
- displayname: The name displayed in the UI (e.g., first and
last name).
- description: String information representing detailed
information for use in the UI. It can be freely edited
by the user.
- email: The user's email address information. Either a string
in the form of an email address or an empty string is allowed.
- groups: A list of strings. Used to manage user roles. A user
can be assigned to multiple groups.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was
    not executed due to lack of access rights.

get.description:
Returns information on the specified user name in dictionary
format.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group or users belonging to the operator or
guest group modifying their own accounts.
The user name must be specified in the path.

If the specified user name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If an unauthorized user attempts to execute
this API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the user information was read correctly, it returns the
same information as shown in `Read All User Information`.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was
    not executed due to lack of access rights.

404.description:
**E2201** Not Found.
    The account specified by the user was not found.

put.description:
Update the existing user information.

This operation can be performed by either admin or the
operator or guest with the specified user name.
The existing user name must be specified in the path.
The request body must be in JSON format containing
the following keys. If you do not want to update
an element, specify null.
- displayname (Optional[str]): The name displayed
in the UI (e.g., first and last name). A string of
one or more characters must be specified.
- disabled (Optional[bool]): True to disable the account, false to enable the account.
Users cannot disable their own account.
- description (Optional[str]): String information
representing detailed information for use in the UI.
It can be freely edited by the user. If you do not
want it to be displayed, specify an empty string.
- password (Optional[str]): Specify a user password
between 8 and 256 characters.
- email (Optional[str]): User's e-mail address.
Incorrect formatting will result in an error. Be
sure to specify it.
- language (Literal['en', 'jp']): User language
preferences. Currently only English and Japanese are
supported, but more options will be added in the future.
- nav_path (Optional[str]): User default page.
Only Admin account can modify Guest account navigation path.

If the specified user name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If an unauthorized user attempts to
execute this API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the user information was updated correctly,
it returns true.

404.description:
**E2201** Not Found.
    The account specified by the user was not found.

post.description:
Creates a new user.
**This API is currently disabled. Whenever it is run,
it returns a 405 error.**

Only users who belong to the admin group can perform this
operation.
The new user name must be specified in the path.
The request body must be in JSON format containing
the following keys.
- displayname (str): The name displayed in the UI (e.g., first and
last name). A string of one or more characters must be specified.
- description (str): String information representing detailed
information for use in the UI. It can be freely edited
by the user. If you do not want it to be displayed, specify an
empty string.
- password (str): Specify a user password between 8 and 256
characters.
- email (str): User's e-mail address. Incorrect formatting
will result in an error. Be sure to specify it.
- language (Literal['en', 'jp']): User language preferences.
Currently only English and Japanese are supported, but more
options will be added in the future.
- groups (List[str]): Specifies a list of groups to which the user
belongs. Multiple groups can be specified.

If the specified user name already exists, a 409 error is
responded. If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this
API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the user information was created correctly, it returns the
same information as shown in `Read All User Information`,
except that the password is not hashed.

delete.description:
Delete the specified user.
**This API is currently disabled. Whenever it is run,
it returns a 405 error.**

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group or users belonging to the operator
group modifying their own accounts.
The existing user name must be specified in the path.

If the specified user name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If the specified user is `admin`, a 403 error
is responded since this default account is not allowed to
delete or modify. If an unauthorized user attempts to
execute this API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the user information was deleted correctly,
it returns true.

get.description:
Reads all token account information registered in this device.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group or M2M authentication.
No parameters are required for this request.

Reads all currently registered token information from a file
and returns it in dictionary format. The keys of the
dictionary are user names and the values are user information.
User information includes the following:
- accounttype: Indicates whether the account is user or token
information. Since this API handles only token information,
token is always returned.
- creation: The date and time the token was created.
- expire: Accounts that expire after this time are
automatically deactivated. Accounts with no expiration date will
be displayed as `perpetual`.
- disabled: True if the account is disabled, false if the
account is enabled.
- description: String information representing detailed
information for use in the UI. It can be freely edited
by the user.
- email: The token's email address information. Either a string
in the form of an email address or an empty string is allowed.
- groups: A list of strings. Used to manage user roles. A token
can be assigned to multiple groups.

If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this API, a 403
error will be returned.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was
    not executed due to lack of access rights.

post.description:
Creates a new token.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group.
The request body must be in JSON format containing
the following keys.
- description (str): String information representing detailed
information for use in the UI. It can be freely edited
by the user. If you do not want it to be displayed, specify an
empty string.
- expire (datetime): Specify the expiration date.
If no expiration date is specified, specify `perpetual`.
- disabled (bool): True to disable the account,
false to enable the account.

If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this API, a 403
error will be returned.
To avoid duplicate token names, the server repeats naming
with uuid up to a certain number of times until a unique name
is created. Therefore, the probability of a 409 error is
astronomically small.
If the token information was created correctly, it returns the
same information as shown in `Read All Token Information`,
except that the password is not hashed.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was
    not executed due to lack of access rights.

409.description:
**E2202** Conflict.
    The account specified by the user already exists.

get.description:
Returns information on the specified token name in dictionary
format.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group.
If the specified token name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this
API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the token information was read correctly, it returns the
same information as shown in `Read All Token Information`.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was
    not executed due to lack of access rights.

404.description:
**E2201** Not Found.
    The account specified by the user was not found.

put.description:
Update the existing token information.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group.
The existing token name must be specified in the path.
The request body must be in JSON format containing
the following keys. If you do not want to update
an element, specify null.
- description (Optional[str]): String information
representing detailed information for use in the UI.
It can be freely edited by the user. If you do not
want it to be displayed, specify an empty string.
- disabled (Optional[bool]): True to disable the account,
false to enable the account.

If the specified token name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If user tries to change the disabled property of
an expired token to False, the process fails with a 403 error.
If an unauthorized user attempts to execute this API, a 403
error will be returned.
If the token information was updated correctly,
it returns true.

404.description:
**E2201** Not Found.
    The account specified by the user was not found.

delete.description:
Delete the specified token.

This operation can be performed only by users belonging
to the admin group.
The existing token name must be specified in the path.

If the specified token name does not exist, a 404 error is
responded. If an unauthorized user attempts to execute
this API, a 403 error will be returned.
If the token information was deleted correctly,
it returns true.

403.description:
**E2209** Forbidden.
    The user attempted to run user APIs, but was

404.description:
**E2201** Not Found.
    The account specified by the user was not found.

get.description:
Get the current system clock time.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it 
returns the current time.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

post.description:
Change the current system clock time.

The request body must be in JSON format containing 
the following keys.
- `set_time`(datetime, optional): Absolute time for the time 
specification. Valid only when `relative` is `false`.
- `set_timedelta`(timedelta, optional): Relative time for the
time specification. Valid only when `relative` is `true`.
- `relative`(boolean): If `true`, the passed `set_timedelta` 
will be added to the current system time. If `false`, the 
current system time will be set to the passed `set_time` value.

For the formats of values accepted as datetime and timedelta 
types, see the 
[Pydantic documentation](https://docs.pydantic.dev/usage/types/#datetime-types).

This API allows the user to specify the absolute time to 
change the system time, or to specify amount of time to be 
advanced or set back the current system time.
If `relative` is `true`, `set_timedelta` must be specified
and `set_time` will be ignored. If `relative` is `false`, 
`set_time` must be specified and `set_timedelta` will be 
ignored. `relative` is `false` by default.
If NTP is enabled and the system time is synchronized to the 
network, disable NTP first, as the time cannot be changed.

If the request is successfully processed, it 
returns the current time after setting.

405.description:
**E2602** Method Not Allowed.
    The user attempted to change time even though NTP is
    enabled on the device.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

get.description:
Get the currently configured system time zone.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it 
returns the current time zone.

200.description: The time zone currently set for the device

500.description:
**E2612** Internal Server Error.
    The server tried to get the available timezone list by 
    `ListTimezones()` method of `org.freedesktop.timedate1`, but 
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.

post.description:
Change the system time zone.

The request body must be in JSON format containing 
the following key.
- `timezone`(string): time zone represented in IANA 
(Olson) format, e.g. `Asia/Tokyo`.

A list of configurable time zones can be obtained 
via the other API.

If the request is successfully processed, it 
returns the current time zone.

400.description:
**E2601** Bad Request. 
    The user specified a timezone not in the configurable list 
    for the device.

500.description:
**E2610** Internal Server Error.
    The server tried to set the system timezone by 
    `SetTimezone()` method of `org.freedesktop.timedate1`, but 
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.

get.summary: Get List of Configurable Time Zones
get.description:
Get a list of time zones can be set to the system.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it 
returns a list of time zones known on the 
local system as an array of names.

200.description: The time zone currently set for the device

500.description:
**E2612** Internal Server Error.
    The server tried to get the available timezone list by 
    `ListTimezones()` method of `org.freedesktop.timedate1`, but 
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.

get.description:
Check the NTP status of the device.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it
returns following information as boolean values.

- `enabled`: Whether a service to perform time 
synchronization over the network is enabled by 
configuration or not.
- `synced`: Whether the system time is 
synchronized with the network time.
- `available`: Whether a service to perform time 
synchronization over the network is available.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

post.description:
Enables or disables the service that performs 
time synchronization on the network.  

The request body must be in JSON format containing
the following key.
- `use_ntp`(boolean): Whether or not to use the 
time synchronization service.

If the request is successfully processed, 
following information after the update
is returned as boolean values.

- `enabled`: Whether a service to perform time
synchronization over the network is enabled by
configuration or not.
- `synced`: Whether the system time is
synchronized with the network time.
- `available`: Whether a service to perform time
synchronization over the network is available.

405.description:
**E2603** Method Not Allowed.
    The user attempted to enable NTP even though NTP is not 
    available on the device.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

get.description:
Show overall status of the device network.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it
returns following information.
- `state`: The current overall networking state.
See the
[definitions](https://developer-old.gnome.org/NetworkManager/stable/nm-dbus-types.html#NMState)
for details.
- `connectivity`: The result of the last connectivity
check. See the
[definitions](https://developer-old.gnome.org/NetworkManager/stable/nm-dbus-types.html#NMConnectivityState)
for details.
- `wifi_hw`: `True` if Wi-Fi hardware is available,
`False` otherwise.
- `wifi`: `True` if Wi-Fi is enabled, `False` otherwise.
- `wwan_hw`: `True` if WWAN hardware is available,
`False` otherwise.
- `wwan`: `True` if WWAN is enabled, `False` otherwise.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

get.description:
Show the current device hostname.

The request can be made with the following query
parameters.
- `short`(bool): If `True`, it returns the
hostname without the domain name. Default is `False`.

If the request is successfully processed, it
returns the hostname as a string value.

500.description:
**E2707** Internal Server Error.
    The server tried to get the machine hostname
    by reading `Hostname` property of
    `org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.Settings`,
    but D-Bus responded to the request with an
    error message.

get.description:
Show status of managed devices.

No parameters are required for this request.

If the request is successfully processed, it
returns a list of managed device statuses
which contains following information.
- `device`: The device name.
- `type`: The general type of the network
device; i.e. Ethernet, Wi-Fi, etc. See the
[definitions](https://developer-old.gnome.org/NetworkManager/stable/nm-dbus-types.html#NMDeviceType)
for details.
- `state`: The current state of the device.
See the
[definitions](https://developer-old.gnome.org/NetworkManager/stable/nm-dbus-types.html#NMDeviceState)
for details.
- `connection`: If an active connection setting
is associated with a device, the name of that
connection is displayed. Returns `None` if it
is not associated.
- `interface_type`: The type of interface for the device. Can be PRIMARY, SECONDARY, SWITCH, WIFI, LTE, or UNKNOWN.

500.description:
Internal Server Error.
    D-Bus responded to the request with an error message.
    Status code is used only when the status number from 
    the AI Box D-Bus server needs to be sent to the client.

get.description:
Show detailed information about the specified
device.

The device name must be specified in the path.

If the specified device name does not exist,
a 404 error is responded. Also, the detailed

get.description:
Diagnoses the correct operation of this microservice
in real-time to the extent possible.
(Some functions, such as rebooting, cannot be
inspected directly because a real reboot would
affect service delivery.)
This API is intended to be used internally and regularly
by Docker's
[HEALTHCHECK](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#healthcheck)
function.

This diagnosis includes the following tests.
- **Test 1**. Reboot: Check `CanReboot` returns "yes".
- **Test 2**. Time: Check ListTimezones returns a list
contains "UTC".
- **Test 3**. Network: Check that one or more devices
can be detected.
- **Test 4**. User: Check that admin user can be loaded.
- **Test 5**. Device: Check that aibox-dbus-server is
accessible.

No parameters are required for this request.

The response will contain the following information:
- **healthy**: `true` if all tests are passed,
`false` otherwise.
- **test_reboot**: `true` if CanReboot returned "yes",
`false` otherwise.
- **test_timezone**: `true` if ListTimezones returns
a list contains "UTC", `false` otherwise.
- **test_network**: `true` if one or more devices can
be detected, `false` otherwise.
- **test_users**: `true` if admin can be loaded,
`false` otherwise.
- **test_device**: `true` if healthcheck command
successfully executed, `false` otherwise.
Always returns 200 OK to detect session expiration.

Checks if the device can be rebooted.

No parameters are required for this request.

When requested, one of the following four values will be responded.

- **yes**: The operation is supported and the user may
execute the operation without further authentication.
- **no**: The operation is available but the user is not
allowed to execute the operation.
- **challenge**: The operation is available but only after
authorization.
- **na**: The operation is not available because hardware,
kernel, or drivers do not support it.

These values are based on
[this manual](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/org.freedesktop.login1.html#Methods),
but this API cannot reboot the device if a response other
than **yes** is given.

Remote access providers enable secure connections to the device from external networks.
This includes services like Cloudflare tunnels and other remote connectivity solutions.

post.summary: Create a new remote access provider
post.description:
Create and configure a new remote access provider.

**Parameters:**
- **provider**: The type of remote provider to create
- **request_body**: Configuration details for the provider

**Common Request Body Fields (apply to all providers):**
- **active** (boolean, required): Whether to activate the provider immediately after creation
- **custom_name** (string, optional): Human-readable name for this provider instance (must be unique across all providers)

**Provider-Specific Fields:**
- **tunnel_token** (string): Authentication token - see provider details below
- **tunnel_domain** (string): Custom domain configuration - see provider details below

**Supported Providers:**

**Cloudflare Provider** ✅ Fully Supported
- `tunnel_token`: **Required** - Cloudflare Tunnel token for authentication
- `tunnel_domain`: Not used (Cloudflare manages domain automatically)
- Example: `{"active": true, "tunnel_token": "your-token", "custom_name": "prod-cloudflare"}`

**Device Console Provider** ✅ Fully Supported
- `tunnel_token`: Not used (managed by device agent)
- `tunnel_domain`: Not used (managed by device agent)
- Example: `{"active": true, "custom_name": "main-console"}`

**Ngrok Provider** ⚠️ Not Supported Yet
- This provider type is not yet implemented
- Will return HTTP 501 Not Implemented error

**Remote SSH Provider** ⚠️ Not Supported Yet
- This provider type is not yet implemented
- Will return HTTP 501 Not Implemented error

**Returns:**
- Provider UUID for future operations
- Success status and confirmation message

**Notes:**
- Only provide fields that are used by the provider type (omit unused fields)
- The `custom_name` must be unique across all provider types
- Activating a provider will attempt to establish the connection immediately
- Some providers require specific tokens/credentials to function properly

post.summary: Create a new DNS access provider
post.description:
Create and configure a new DNS access provider.

DNS providers allow access through custom domain names that you control,
as opposed to automatically generated tunnel URLs.

**Parameters:**
- **provider**: The type of DNS provider to create
- **request_body**: Configuration details for the provider

**Request Body Fields:**
- **active** (boolean, required): Whether to activate the provider immediately after creation
- **domain** (string, optional): The custom domain name to use for access
- **custom_name** (string, optional): Human-readable name for this provider instance (must be unique across all providers)

**Provider-Specific Field Usage:**

**Custom Domain Provider:**
- `active`: Controls activation state
- `domain`: **Recommended** - Your custom domain name (e.g., "mydevice.example.com")
  - Must be a valid fully qualified domain name
  - You must configure DNS records externally to point to your device
  - Minimum 2 labels required (e.g., "example.com" is valid, "example" is not)
  - Maximum 255 characters
  - Only alphanumeric characters and hyphens allowed in labels
- `custom_name`: Optional - Unique identifier for this provider instance

**Returns:**
- Provider UUID for future operations
- Success status and confirmation message

**Notes:**
- The `custom_name` must be unique across all provider types
- DNS provider does not establish tunnels; it only manages domain configurations
- You are responsible for ensuring DNS records point to the correct IP address
- The domain will be applied to dependent Docker containers when activated

put.description:
Update the configuration of an existing DNS access provider.

**Parameters:**
- **provider_identifier**: The unique identifier (UUID) or custom_name of the DNS provider to update

**Request Body Fields (all optional):**
- **active** (boolean, optional): Set to true to activate, false to deactivate the provider
- **domain** (string, optional): Update the custom domain name configuration
- **custom_name** (string, optional): Update the human-readable name (must be unique across all providers)

**Provider-Specific Field Usage:**

**Custom Domain Provider:**
- `active`: Toggle activation state
  - When activated, the domain is applied to dependent Docker containers
  - When deactivated, the domain configuration is removed from containers
- `domain`: Update the custom domain name
  - Must be a valid fully qualified domain name (FQDN)
  - Minimum 2 labels required (e.g., "example.com" is valid, "example" is not)
  - Maximum 255 characters
  - Only alphanumeric characters and hyphens allowed in labels
  - You must ensure DNS records point to the correct IP address
- `custom_name`: Update the unique identifier for this provider instance

**Returns:**
- Updated provider UUID
- Success status and confirmation message

**Notes:**
- Only include fields you want to update (all fields are optional)
- The `custom_name` must be unique across all provider types
- Changing the domain while active will update running containers
- DNS provider manages domain configuration but does not handle actual DNS records
